Thought: Interim report with deliberate pending placeholders for human O1 audit. Strong provenance/pre-registration design and candor; but no human-validated accuracy, low HGVS recall, pilot audits missed the 2% target, gatekeeper rate uninformative, dense/overlong, single-team self-built evaluation.
Summary: GP-RareLink describes a provenance-first pipeline (SLIDERS-style, Claude Opus extraction with verbatim quotes, three-state HPO, Claude gatekeeper, GA4GH phenopackets) run under a frozen pre-registration on six rare diseases (plus six beside them), scored against held-out ClinVar and OMIM. It reports full quote coverage, low gatekeeper-unsupported shares (0.43% pooled), low HGVS recall against ClinVar (10-35% tier 1), 57% recovery of OMIM allelic variants bounded by open-access coverage, and 269 gap candidates awaiting adjudication. The primary human audit (250 claims, 2% target), triage, adjudication and bias arm are pending; two pilot audits found 6.0% and 6.3% unsupported.
Strengths: Rigorous design discipline: frozen pre-registration, isolation test keeping ClinVar/OMIM out of extraction, pre-drawn seeded audit sample, explicit rule C with operating characteristics and exact intervals.
Unusual candor: states the gatekeeper share is not an error rate, reports unfavorable pilot audits, low recall, open-weight comparison and 16 limitations.

Useful held-out evaluation: ClinVar concordance plus OMIM holdout, with the finding that literature access rather than reading is the binding constraint on recall; tier definitions and recall/overlap distinction are clear.
Reproducibility: seeds, pinned ontologies/tools, dated snapshots, scripted human-results filling; three-state phenotypes and per-value provenance are well suited to curation.
Open-weight comparison under identical scaffold gives a concrete, if narrow, cost and quality contrast.
Weaknesses: The central claim, accuracy a person can verify, is untested: the primary O1 audit, triage, adjudication, bias (O4) and efficiency (O5) results are all pending, while the only human data (two single-rater pilot audits on the development disease) missed the 2% target. The paper therefore supports provenance and feasibility, not accuracy.

The headline automated numbers are weakly informative: the Claude gatekeeper's 0.43% unsupported share is a same-family model reading that the authors' own pilot shows missed most human-found errors (2 of 6, 1 of 4) and that disagrees with the PI labels in both directions (26 of 65 removed claims were unsupported); 'all values have a verbatim quote' only shows the quote exists, not that it supports the value. HGVS recall of 10-35% and 57% OMIM recovery are not interpretable as accuracy until misses are triaged, and no baseline (e.g. LitVar, AVADA, a single-pass LLM, or an ablation of the gatekeeper) shows what the pipeline adds.

Evaluation validity and independence concerns: HA20 is the development disease and 92 of 160 papers were ClinVar-seeded; ClinVar/OMIM are imperfect and partly circular with the corpus; open access covers only 14-53% of papers; memorization probe is black-box with only 10 post-cutoff papers; calibration set formed by a rule with two post-label amendments and labelled by one PI; Claude Code built, ran and drafted the study, and the PI-labelled reference is single-rater. Deduplication is weak (6 of 93 false merges in pilot, 9 of 38 papers with differing counts).

Presentation: the paper is extremely dense, mixes registered, extension, exploratory and addendum studies with many internal decision codes (D-nn) and run names, and is long on procedure relative to results; main text is hard to follow and several key results live in appendices.

Licensing and reproducibility loose ends: tags and OSF registration not yet pushed, manifests record only an alias, unredacted transcripts remain in public history, and no licence for outputs containing verbatim quotes is settled.
Questions: What gatekeeper sensitivity against human labels will you report, and how will the 2% claim be interpreted if rule C passes with an upper bound near 2.9%?
How does the pipeline compare with a simple one-pass Claude extraction without gatekeeper, and with LitVar/AVADA on the same papers?
How will ClinVar-cited and ClinVar-seeded papers be handled so concordance is not inflated or deflated by corpus construction?
What fraction of low HGVS recall will triage attribute to extraction error versus ClinVar citation artifacts?
How will rater non-independence from the gatekeeper's reasoning and the volunteer calibration floor affect audit validity?
Limitations: Authors list 16 limitations candidly; main additional ones are single-model-family extraction and judging, open-access-only corpus, and reliance on a single PI for the calibration reference.
